title: Mars Opens Hyderabad GCC With Genpact for AI Expansion
summary: Mars launches its Hyderabad Global Capability Center in partnership with Genpact to advance digital transformation and AI capabilities across operations.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Mars Incorporated launched its Hyderabad Global Capability Center in partnership with Genpact to scale digital and AI operations across the enterprise.
- The GCC will focus on advanced analytics, machine learning, automation, and cloud infrastructure to support Mars's global business transformation.
- This move positions Hyderabad as a strategic AI hub for Mars, tapping into India's deep tech talent pool and innovation ecosystem.


Mars Incorporated has officially opened its Global Capability Center (GCC) in Hyderabad, India, marking a significant expansion of the company's digital and artificial intelligence operations. The facility, launched in partnership with global professional services leader Genpact, will serve as a strategic hub for advanced analytics, machine learning, and enterprise automation initiatives across Mars's worldwide operations.


## Strategic Partnership With Genpact


The collaboration with Genpact brings together Mars's consumer goods expertise with Genpact's proven track record in digital transformation and AI implementation. Genpact will provide operational support, technical infrastructure, and talent development resources to accelerate the GCC's capabilities. The partnership model allows Mars to leverage Genpact's existing AI platforms and frameworks while building proprietary systems tailored to the food and pet care giant's specific business needs.


According to industry observers, this co-development approach reduces time to value compared to building capabilities entirely in-house. The GCC will house data scientists, machine learning engineers, cloud architects, and business analysts working on projects spanning supply chain optimization, consumer insights, and product innovation.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 13, 2026, the Hyderabad GCC is now operational with an initial team focused on establishing core infrastructure and pilot projects. Mars plans to scale the facility's headcount significantly over the next 18 months as key systems move into production. The center will operate 24/7 to support Mars's global markets across multiple time zones.


## AI and Digital Transformation Focus


The GCC's primary mandate centers on deploying AI-driven solutions across four key domains:


- **Supply chain intelligence:** Predictive analytics for demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and logistics routing using real-time data from Mars's manufacturing and distribution networks.
- **Consumer analytics:** Machine learning models to analyze purchasing behavior, sentiment data, and market trends across Mars's portfolio of brands including M&M's, Snickers, Pedigree, and Whiskas.
- **Automation and efficiency:** Robotic process automation (RPA) and intelligent workflow systems to streamline back-office operations, finance, and human resources functions.
- **Cloud modernization:** Migration of legacy systems to cloud-native architectures with integrated AI services for real-time decision support.


The center will also serve as an innovation lab for exploring emerging technologies like generative AI for creative development, computer vision for quality control, and natural language processing for customer service automation.


## Why Hyderabad as the Location


Mars's choice of Hyderabad reflects the city's established reputation as a premier technology and AI talent hub in India. The region hosts major GCCs for global enterprises including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and dozens of Fortune 500 companies. Hyderabad offers a deep pool of engineering and data science graduates from institutions like the International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) campuses.


The city's robust digital infrastructure, favorable business environment, and cost advantages make it an attractive location for enterprises seeking to scale AI capabilities without the overhead of traditional Western tech hubs. Mars joins a growing list of consumer goods and manufacturing companies establishing dedicated AI centers in the region.


## What This Means


The Mars Hyderabad GCC launch signals the company's commitment to AI-driven transformation across its global operations. By partnering with Genpact and tapping into India's tech ecosystem, Mars is positioning itself to compete more effectively in an increasingly data-driven consumer goods landscape. The facility's success could serve as a blueprint for other multinational corporations seeking to accelerate digital capabilities through strategic offshore partnerships. For Hyderabad, the center reinforces the city's status as a critical node in the global AI talent and innovation network.
